There are plenty of good reasons why so many Cibolo homeowners are starting to replace their conventional HVAC systems with heat pump technology. One of the most important reasons is simplicity. With conventional HVACs, your home needs an air conditioning system and a separate furnace or electric resistance heating system to ensure comfort all year round. Having such a complex array of heating and cooling equipment means more frequent maintenance and a higher likelihood of equipment failure. A heat pump, on the other hand, provides both heating and cooling for your home. That means you’ll have just a single system to maintain and, therefore, you’ll enjoy reliable year-round operation.

After hearing about all of the benefits that a heat pump can offer, homeowners often ask how these devices are able to outperform conventional HVAC systems. The secret lies in their mode of operation. A heat pump, like an air conditioner, carries heat from one place to another. In the summer, it absorbs heat from the air inside your home and carries it outside, cooling your home in the process. In the winter, it works in reverse, capturing heat energy from the outside air and carrying it inside to heat your home. As a result, heat pumps can operate at up to 400% efficiency in heating mode. In air conditioning mode, heat pumps employ variable-speed motors to use exactly as much energy as they need to cool your home. That helps them to outperform most conventional air conditioning systems, too.
